subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Session Architecture: Shared LLM + Isolated Sessions + Public Knowledge Base

question: Should this RFC remain the broad core architecture umbrella, or should maintainers close/supersede it after routing the remaining work to narrower topic-family, WebChat session-management, and memory-boundary trackers?
rationale: Current main partially implements the requested primitives, but the remaining shared-memory, session-family, routing, UI, migration, and security behavior requires maintainer product/security intent before implementation.

options.title: Keep Umbrella And Split
options.body: Keep this issue open for cross-cutting architecture decisions while directing implementation to narrower protocol/store, UI, routing, and memory-security follow-ups.

options.title: Supersede By Narrow Trackers
options.body: Close this broad RFC after confirming https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/90916 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/27526 cover all remaining accepted work.

options.title: Narrow To Routing Only
options.body: Retitle or reinterpret the issue around the remaining channel/session routing boundary and leave public knowledge and WebUI product work to separate issues.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella And Split
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for cross-cutting architecture decisions while directing implementation to narrower protocol/store, UI, routing, and memory-security follow-ups.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the clearest routing/product history and are already connected to adjacent canonical-tracker decisions.
